Synopsis:
Chicago Fed President Goolsbee notes July CPI/PPI prints came in milder than expected, calling recent inflation data "a little better." PCE sits at 3.7% (down from 4.1% May peak), still well above the 2% target. The Fed held rates at 3.50–3.75% last meeting, though 5+ policymakers pushed for a hike. Goolsbee is cautiously optimistic that fading tariff and Iran war oil-price pressures could resume the disinflationary path ("golden path"), but stresses the economy is in a "delicate space." Markets have largely repriced out near-term rate hike expectations following the softer data trio (jobs + CPI + PPI).
